title: Wahoo McDaniel: OU Punt Record Holder Turned Wrestling Star
question: Which former Oklahoma Sooner played in the AFL and became a pro wrestling Hall of Famer?
answer: Wahoo McDaniel, who owns Oklahoma's longest punt at 91 yards, played in the AFL for four teams and then became a pro wrestling star. WWE inducted him into its Hall of Fame Legacy wing in 2019.
summary: Wahoo McDaniel booted Oklahoma's longest punt, 91 yards in 1958, then played in the AFL and became a five-time NWA U.S. wrestling champion.
body: Edward Hugh McDaniel, better known as Wahoo, was a Choctaw-Chickasaw athlete who played football for Oklahoma before building one of the most unusual careers any former Sooner has had. His nickname came from his father, an avid fisherman known as Big Wahoo.

His name is still on a Sooner record. On November 8, 1958, Oklahoma beat Iowa State 20-0 in Ames, and the school's record book credits McDaniel with a 91-yard punt in that game. Nearly seven decades later it remains the longest punt in the program's history, ahead of Joe Wylie's 87-yarder in 1970.

After Oklahoma he played in the American Football League, suiting up for the Houston Oilers, Denver Broncos, New York Jets and Miami Dolphins. He was on the Oilers team that won the first AFL championship game after the 1960 season, and he hit hard enough as a linebacker to build a following of his own.

Wrestling ran alongside football from the start. He debuted in 1961 and left football for the ring full time in 1969. Known for his chop, he won the NWA United States Heavyweight Championship five times and became a major draw in the Mid-Atlantic territory and beyond. He died April 18, 2002, at age 63.
WWE inducted him into its Hall of Fame Legacy wing in 2019, a fitting honor for a Sooner who made his mark in two very different arenas.
